pk.context: 1000 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: Gut bacteria split this 1950 anti-inflammatory into two products, one of which is much less well absorbed.

clues.text: Less than 15% of an oral dose is absorbed as parent drug, and it is over 99.3% bound to albumin. Intestinal bacteria break it down, and its products are mainly eliminated in the urine.
The parent compound has a molecular weight of 398.4 and is an azo compound of salicylic acid.
Approved under an NDA as 500 mg tablets, with a delayed-release form also listed.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated in intestinal or urinary obstruction, porphyria, and hypersensitivity to sulfonamides or salicylates; nausea and headache are among the most common reactions.
Mild to moderate ulcerative colitis, adjunctive therapy in severe cases, and prolonging remission between acute attacks.
Classed as an anti-inflammatory agent, it is split by intestinal bacteria, and most of its 5-aminosalicylic acid part stays in the colon.
The generic name begins with S and has thirteen letters.
